name: Evidence anchors high-stakes law and policy
plainSummary: When laws or rules seriously affect health, safety, or freedom, they should align with the best available evidence and expert consensus when that exists.
whyRoot: When mistakes are costly and hard to reverse, guessing is a poor basis for coercion. Anchoring high-stakes rules to the best shared picture of facts is a root commitment: it reduces arbitrary harm and makes public justification possible.
description: Foundational commitment that when laws or regulations materially affect health, safety, or liberty, they should align with credible empirical and expert consensus where such evidence exists.
